validation.notes: Repair: DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions in packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts forced project trust ON (setProjectTrusted(true)) for the pre-trust bootstrap pass, so project-local extensions were resolved and loaded before any trust decision. Minimal change: one argument flipped to setProjectTrusted(false); the following settingsManager.reload() now also reloads settings in the untrusted state. Regression (.prale-eval/regression.mjs, node:assert/strict, no deps/network) drives the real loader lifecycle through .prale-eval/subject.mjs with initialTrusted=true and asserts: (a) the first settings mutation of reload() is ['set', false]; (b) every package resolve() during bootstrap observed loadedTrust=false; (c) the pre-trust extension set the resolveProjectTrust callback receives contains user.ts and cli.ts but NOT project.ts; (d) the trust decisions observed are [forced false, resolved decision] and the final getExtensions() is user+cli when trust is declined and user+project+cli when approved; (e) a direct loadProjectTrustExtensions() call (twice, idempotent) also yields only cli.ts+user.ts and forces untrusted first. Exit code 0 on the repaired source. Negative control: with the original fault restored (setProjectTrusted(true)) the same command fails with AssertionError 'bootstrap must force untrusted project settings first, got ["set",true]' and the trace shows the leak ['extensions',['cli.ts','user.ts','project.ts']] -> exit 1. Environment: Node v24.14.0 (stripTypeScriptTypes + vm SourceTextModule, experimental warnings only). No full-project typecheck/test run was possible: node_modules is not installed in this workspace and dependency installation is out of scope, so validation is limited to this SSV/VM-based regression against the real source; no fixture files (.fixtures/) were required.
